hook: Human brain organoids sustained more than 5 years.

body.voiceover: Harvard reports that Paola Arlotta's lab sustained human brain organoids more than 5 years — 3 times the previous record of 694 days — in findings published in Nature. The team examined 34 organoids at 8 timepoints. When cells of different ages were combined, older ones immediately made neurons normally produced 2 or 3 months later. They concluded the cells retain a memory of steps already performed. Arlotta called it a proof of principle.

motion.what: Human brain organoids sustained in culture more than 5 years, past the 694-day record
motion.how: 34 organoids sampled by single-cell RNA sequencing at 8 timepoints; cells of different ages combined in one organoid
motion.impact: Older progenitors immediately made later-stage neurons, which the researchers read as a memory of developmental steps already performed

body.voiceover: A bioRxiv preprint describes ProteinTalks, a neural ordinary differential equation foundation model built from over 38 million perturbed protein measurements in breast cancer cell lines. The authors report it predicts drug efficacy and synergy, flags resistance-associated proteins, and offers a basis for virtual cells.

motion.who: Rui Sun, Tiannan Guo and colleagues
motion.what: ProteinTalks, a neural ordinary differential equation foundation model for virtual cell construction
motion.how: Pretrained on over 38 million perturbed protein measurements generated in breast cancer cell lines
motion.impact: Authors report predicted drug efficacy and synergy, resistance-associated proteins, and xenograft drug responses

body.voiceover: Also on bioRxiv, Oxford researchers posted SPOT, a shape, appearance and motion phenotype tool. They report applying it to over 1.6 million organoid instances, and that altered WNT signaling — not mutant RAS or p53 — predisposes intestinal organoids to irregular morphogenesis.

motion.who: Felix Y. Zhou, Xin Lu and colleagues
motion.what: Shape-Appearance-Motion phenome plus SPOT, described as an image-transcriptome and its analyzer
motion.how: Applied to a simulated organoid database with known ground-truth and over 1.6 million mouse and human organoid instances from 2D projection videos
motion.impact: With single-cell RNA sequencing, altered WNT signaling, not mutant RAS or p53, predisposed intestinal organoids to irregular morphogenesis

body.voiceover: Turning to regulators: Emulate announced it submitted its full FDA ISTAND qualification package for the Human Liver-Chip, covering drug-induced liver injury. It cites reproducibility across 3 laboratories and 3 hepatocyte donors. Qualification, Emulate says, would set a regulatory precedent.

motion.what: Full FDA ISTAND qualification package submitted for the Human Liver-Chip as a drug development tool for drug-induced liver injury assessment
motion.how: Data from the Zoë Culture Module plus, for the first time in the process, the AVA Emulation System
motion.impact: Emulate says qualification would set a regulatory precedent for Organ-on-a-Chip liver toxicity testing

body.voiceover: CDER publishes a table inventorying drug development contexts where it's open to streamlined nonclinical programs, including NAMs. For anticancer drugs warranting QT assessment, it says hiPSC-CM studies following best practices can replace an animal study. Sponsors are encouraged to discuss proposals.

motion.who: FDA Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
motion.what: Inventory table of drug development contexts open to streamlined nonclinical programs, including NAMs use
motion.how: Categories span safety pharmacology, general toxicity, carcinogenicity, DART and screens; 505(b)(2), generic and biosimilar pathways excluded
motion.impact: For anticancer pharmaceuticals warranting QT assessment, hiPSC-CM studies following best practices can stand in for an animal study

body.voiceover: In Europe, EMA says it launched a voluntary pilot letting companies, CROs and academic labs submit NAM data outside a marketing authorisation application, with non-binding, non-decisional feedback. Submissions run until the third quarter of 2027, then a lessons-learned report.

onScreen.title: EMA opens voluntary NAM data pilot

motion.what: Voluntary data submission pilot for New Approach Methodologies data
motion.how: Companies, method developers, CROs and academic labs apply, then submit a briefing package assessed by an operational expert group of non-clinical experts
motion.impact: Participants get individual, non-binding, non-decisional feedback; EMA will publish a lessons-learned report at the end

body.voiceover: NIH's Common Fund announced 20 Phase 1 winners of the Complement-ARIE Reduction to Practice Challenge Prize, run with NASA's Tournament Lab. They include CAR-T immunotherapy clinical trials on a chip and AI-integrated human skin immune organoids, all eligible for Phase 2.

motion.who: NIH Common Fund Complement-ARIE program with NASA's Tournament Lab
motion.what: 20 Phase 1 winners of the Reduction to Practice Challenge Prize, eligible for Phase 2
motion.how: Submissions needed a clear intended use plus a plan to reach usable form within the challenge timeframe
motion.impact: Aims at combinatorial NAM platforms that can be submitted to the Validation and Qualification Network managed by the Foundation for NIH

body.voiceover: And finally, FDA, HESI and the Safety Pharmacology Society scheduled a hybrid workshop on ICH S7A and NAMs in safety pharmacology, aiming to build consensus to reopen the guideline. FDA says it won't change guidelines, but will shape future policy.

motion.who: FDA with the Health and Environmental Sciences Institute and the Safety Pharmacology Society
motion.what: Hybrid public workshop on ICH S7A and NAMs in safety pharmacology
motion.how: One-day exchange of real-world case studies between regulators and industry to define discipline-specific NAM use cases for S7A
motion.impact: FDA says it will not change ICH guidelines directly, but the exchange will be pivotal in shaping future regulatory policy
